clue.text: Is it found in POw camp cheddar ?

definitions.text: Is it found in POw camp cheddar ?

parts.words: Is it found in POw camp cheddar ?
parts.note: read one way it asks about something in a prisoner-of-war camp and a cheese; read another it points at the limestone caves of Cheddar Gorge, where mineral columns rise from the floor

explanation.surface: A puzzled question about what turns up in a prison-camp cheese ration.
explanation.walkthrough: Cheddar is a village in Somerset whose gorge is famous for its show caves. The clue also hints at a build-up: STALAG is a German prisoner-of-war camp and a MITE is the tiny creature found in old cheese.
explanation.definitionFit: Limestone caves such as those at Cheddar hold upward-growing mineral pillars formed by dripping water.

clue.text: Ill-humoured ?

parts.note: looks like a word for grumpy, but read as 'humour that is ill' it describes jokes in poor taste, black comedy about disease and death

explanation.definitionFit: Humour described as ill or tasteless is commonly called by the word that also means unwell.

clue.text: An old railway-man on the dole

definitions.note: a phrase describing a person living on charity, standing for the noun naming such a person

parts.note: the article gives the single letter A
the LMS was the London, Midland and Scottish Railway, one of Britain's pre-nationalisation companies, so its worker is an LMS man

explanation.surface: A retired railway worker now living on benefits.
explanation.walkthrough: The LMS (London, Midland and Scottish Railway) was a British railway company merged away in 1948, hence 'old'.
explanation.definitionFit: An almsman is a person supported by charitable handouts, so someone kept by others' giving.

clue.text: It's debasing for a full-grown oriental sailor

parts.note: a full-grown person or animal is an adult
E, for east, is the crossword abbreviation for oriental
a rating is a sailor below officer rank in the navy

explanation.surface: A remark that it is degrading for a grown-up Eastern seaman to do something.
explanation.definitionFit: To adulterate is to make impure by mixing in inferior matter, so debasing it.

clue.text: In the middle of a dim alley

annotationWithheld.why: In the middle of a dim alley (8): 'dim alley' is an exact anagram of the answer, but no clue word signals the anagram ('of a' cannot), so the fodder has no indicator
annotationWithheld.clue: In the middle of a dim alley

clue.text: Real indoor sport

parts.note: looks like a claim that some indoor game is genuine, but 'real' names the old court game played indoors, the ancestor of the lawn version

explanation.definitionFit: Real tennis, the historic racket game, is played inside a walled court, as at Hampton Court.

clue.text: It took a bashing rather than a mashing from the troops

definitions.text: It took a bashing rather than a mashing from the troops

parts.words: It took a bashing rather than a mashing from the troops
parts.note: soldiers' slang for peeling vegetables in the cookhouse is 'bashing' the item, so the vegetable is bashed, not mashed

explanation.definitionFit: Spud-bashing is British army slang for peeling potatoes, a classic fatigue duty given to soldiers.

clue.text: A soft toy causes little talk

parts.note: p, piano, is the musical direction for soft
a baby's rattle is a toy

explanation.surface: A soft toy that prompts some baby babble.
explanation.walkthrough: 'A' is a link word here; 'causes' joins the wordplay to 'little talk', meaning childish chatter.
explanation.definitionFit: Prattle is childish or trivial chatter, the talk of little ones.

clue.text: It's no longer applied to the late landlord

definitions.meaning: a law or rule still on the books but no longer enforced
post addressed to someone now dead cannot be delivered

explanation.definitionFit: Both senses fit: an unenforced statute, and undeliverable mail, such as a note sent to a deceased landlord.

clue.text: How Italian and German cipher directions become insecure

parts.note: come is Italian for how
und is German for and
a cipher is a zero, written as the letter O
N and E, north and east, are compass directions

explanation.surface: A question about how Italian and German codes for directions become unsafe.
explanation.definitionFit: To come undone is to fall apart or fail, as a loose knot or a person losing composure.

clue.text: Art school doubly approved in Russia

indicators.note: says the piece for Russian approval is given two times over

parts.note: da is the Russian word for yes

explanation.surface: An art movement given the double thumbs-up by Moscow.
explanation.definitionFit: Dada was an early twentieth-century anti-art movement, a school of artists like Duchamp and Arp.

clue.text: Negative description of St. James of Compostela, however

definitions.text: Negative description of St. James of Compostela
definitions.meaning: the saint of Compostela is James the Great, so he was never James the Less, the other apostle
a conjunction meaning all the same

explanation.walkthrough: Two apostles were called James: James the Great (Santiago de Compostela) and James the Less.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means all the same or nonetheless; split into three it denies the saint was 'the Less'.

clue.text: Issue the widow her money, perhaps

indicators.note: signals that the letters for the widow's coin may be rearranged into another form

parts.note: the widow's mite is the small coin given in the Gospel story

explanation.surface: A request to pay a widow what she is owed.
explanation.walkthrough: In the Gospels a poor widow gives her mite, a tiny coin; 'perhaps' rearranges MITE.
explanation.definitionFit: To emit is to send out or give off, so to issue.

clue.text: Baba's potty about food

parts.note: Ali Baba of the Arabian Nights, so the name paired with Baba
potty is British slang for crazy, as is mental

explanation.surface: Someone called Baba is crazy about eating.
explanation.definitionFit: Alimental means relating to nourishment, so concerned with food.

clue.text: Mood of authority

definitions.meaning: a grammatical mood, the form of a verb used for commands
commanding, peremptory, carrying the weight of command

explanation.definitionFit: The command form is a grammatical mood, and the adjective also means commanding or urgent.

clue.text: Baboon in human form

parts.note: a man is a human being
drill is a set routine or form of exercise

explanation.surface: A baboon dressed up as a person.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' joins the definition to the wordplay. A drill is itself a kind of baboon, which helps the surface.
explanation.definitionFit: The mandrill is a large West African primate related to baboons, with a brightly coloured face.

clue.text: It's an order if he's canonized

parts.note: the old subjunctive 'be it so' means 'if it is so', so 'be' stands for if
a man made a saint has St, saint, after him

explanation.surface: Someone says that an instruction comes from a man who has been made a saint.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Be he St' is old-fashioned English for 'if he is a saint'.
explanation.definitionFit: A behest is a command or request given by someone with authority.

clue.text: Interminable parade gets one a decoration, for example

indicators.note: something with no end has had its final letter cut off

parts.note: taken as written before trimming
the Roman numeral for one is I
GM, the George Medal, is a British gallantry decoration

explanation.surface: An endless parade earns someone a medal, for instance.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Interminable' drops the last letter of PARADE; 'gets' and 'for' are link words.
explanation.definitionFit: A paradigm is a model or typical instance of something.

clue.text: Miss Otis's follower decapitated birds

indicators.note: a head cut off means the opening letter is removed

parts.note: Cole Porter's song is 'Miss Otis Regrets', so the word following Miss Otis

explanation.surface: Someone who followed Miss Otis beheaded some birds.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Miss Otis Regrets' is a Cole Porter song in which a woman shoots her lover; dropping the first letter of REGRETS leaves the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Egrets are white wading herons, a family of birds.

clue.text: He serves no territorial purpose

parts.note: seems to describe a useless servant, but means a full-time professional soldier rather than a part-time Territorial Army volunteer

explanation.walkthrough: The Territorial Army was Britain's part-time volunteer reserve, contrasted with the full-time army.
explanation.definitionFit: A regular is a full-time professional soldier, as opposed to a reservist.

clue.text: It's unoriginal yet odd to eat chips

indicators.note: something odd is out of its usual order, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A complaint that eating chips is a copycat habit and strange too.
explanation.walkthrough: 'odd' rearranges EAT CHIPS; 'yet' and 'to' are link words.
explanation.definitionFit: A pastiche is a work imitating another's style, so derivative rather than new.

clue.text: Welcome Italian artist

parts.note: looks like a greeting to a painter from Italy, but 'welcome' in Italian is benvenuto, the first name of a Renaissance goldsmith and sculptor

explanation.definitionFit: Benvenuto Cellini was a Florentine Renaissance goldsmith and sculptor whose first name means welcome.

clue.text: Orator who goes North-east for a guide

indicators.note: the compass letters leaving the word for a guide shows them being removed

parts.note: a cicerone is a guide who shows tourists round sights

explanation.surface: A speaker heads off north-east to find someone to show him round.
explanation.walkthrough: The clue works backwards: add NE to the answer and you get CICERONE, a tourist guide.
explanation.definitionFit: Cicero was the great Roman statesman famed for his speeches.

clue.text: Neat grain-producing country

indicators.note: the letters are worked up to produce something new, signalling a rearrangement

explanation.surface: A nation that grows tidy crops of cereal.
explanation.definitionFit: Argentina is a South American nation.

clue.text: Pa takes her for Spanish food

definitions.note: in Spanish ella is the pronoun for she or her

indicators.note: taking the father figure away from the dish's name shows the letters removed

parts.note: paella is the Spanish rice dish
taken as written

explanation.surface: Dad takes a woman out for a Spanish meal.
explanation.walkthrough: Pa plus the answer makes PAELLA; the definition 'her' is Spanish, in keeping with the theme.
explanation.definitionFit: The Spanish third-person feminine pronoun is ella, meaning she or her.

clue.text: Article on name-dropping

indicators.note: a letter dropped into a word falls inside it, so it is inserted

parts.note: the indefinite article is A
taken as written

explanation.surface: A piece of writing about people who boast of famous acquaintances.
explanation.walkthrough: 'dropping' puts N into A ON; as a whole, an article whose author's name is dropped is unsigned.
explanation.definitionFit: Anon, short for anonymous, labels writing whose author is not named.

clue.text: The thoughts of that fellow Jerome

definitions.text: The thoughts of that fellow Jerome

parts.words: The thoughts of that fellow Jerome
parts.note: refers to Jerome K. Jerome's book 'The ... Thoughts of an ... Fellow', where the missing word describes both thoughts and fellow

explanation.definitionFit: Jerome K. Jerome's essay collection is titled after lazy, aimless thoughts of a lazy man.

clue.text: Fairy takes male celebrity to sunniest spot

parts.note: a peri is a fairy in Persian myth
he is the male pronoun
a lion is a celebrated person, as in literary lion

explanation.surface: A fairy brings a famous man to the sunniest place.
explanation.definitionFit: Perihelion is the point of an orbit closest to the sun, so where it shines most strongly.

clue.text: Antony's requested loan

parts.note: in Julius Caesar, Mark Antony begins 'Friends, Romans, countrymen, lend me your...', asking the crowd to lend their hearing

explanation.definitionFit: Mark Antony asks the crowd to lend him their organs of hearing in Shakespeare's speech.

clue.text: The percentage of officers

definitions.meaning: a fee paid to an agent as a share of a sale
the warrant that appoints an officer in the armed forces

explanation.definitionFit: An agent's cut is a commission, and an officer holds a commission in the forces.
